---
name: Ski alert setup
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner to set up personalized snow
  alerts for ski resorts near them.
---
# Ski alert setup

You watch snow forecasts for the owner's favorite ski resorts and message them when a storm worth skiing is coming. Run this as a friendly chat, one question at a time, and never as a form.

1. Say a short hello, then ask for their zip code. Nothing else first.
2. Look up the ski resorts closest to that zip code (web search is fine). Send a numbered list of the closest 6 to 8 with rough driving distances, and say distances are estimates. Ask which ones they want tracked, and whether they want to add any farther ones.
3. Ask how many inches of new snow should trigger an alert (for example 4 inches or more).
4. Ask how far ahead they want warning (for example 3 to 4 days out) if they haven't said.
5. Ask what time of day they want to be notified. Remember that ski days include weekends, so default to all seven days unless they say otherwise.
6. Save their zip code, chosen resorts, snow threshold, lead time, and notification time as memory.
7. Create one daily routine at their chosen time. The routine checks forecasts (National Weather Service or similar) for each chosen resort over the lead time window and messages the owner in this chat only if at least one resort is forecast to get at least their threshold of new snow. The alert names each qualifying resort, expected total, storm timing, temperature notes, the best day to go, and the forecast issue time. Cross-check big totals against a second source. Do not alert again for the same storm unless the forecast changes a lot. If nothing qualifies, or it is clearly off-season, send nothing, but if the forecast check fails on repeated days, tell the owner.
8. Tell them the exact time saved and that they can change resorts, threshold, or time any time by asking.

routines.name: Ski powder alert
routines.description: Checks daily for incoming snowstorms at the owner's chosen ski resorts and alerts them when the forecast meets their snow threshold.
routines.content:
Check the current weather and snowfall forecasts for the owner's chosen ski resorts (from memory). Use reliable public forecast sources such as National Weather Service point forecasts for each resort's location. Look at the owner's chosen lead-time window (default the next 3 to 4 days). For each resort, estimate expected new snowfall for any incoming storm. Cross-check any big snow total against a second independent source before alerting. Only if at least one resort is forecast to get the owner's snow threshold or more of new snow within the window, send the owner a short, friendly alert naming each qualifying resort, the expected snowfall total, the storm timing, notes on temperature (is it staying cold enough for good snow), the best day to go, and the forecast issue time. Skip resorts below the threshold. Don't alert again for the same storm unless the forecast changes meaningfully. Off-season: if it's clearly too warm for snow or resorts are closed for the season, stay quiet. If the forecast fetch fails on repeated days in a row, tell the owner the check isn't working instead of staying silent. The result goes to the owner in this chat; if no resort meets the threshold and the checks worked, send nothing.
